explanation: I did not search Mathlib for this one; the statement shows on its face that its content belongs to the library. Every main object is the library's own definition: `CuspForm.heckeAlgebra`, `CuspForm.heckeLocal`, `CuspForm.heckeLocal.π`, the Hecke operators `T`/`U`, `ResidualGaloisRep`, `IsAbsolutelyIrreducible`, `IsFrobeniusAt`, `IsNewform`, and so on. The theorem says that the image of `u` under the map `Ψ` between two local Hecke algebras is the image of the U_p operator. The proof never applies a single Mathlib result that could carry this. It relies on the library's own lemmas: `exists_points_jointly_injective_of_charpoly_frobenius_eq_of_isAbsolutelyIrreducible`, `exists_isNewform_of_point_of_up_dvd` and `isLocalHom_and_residue_apply_pi`. It then finishes with a factoring argument in each target local ring, using unit and maximal-ideal facts. Mathlib has none of these Hecke-algebra or modular Galois-representation notions, so it cannot contain this result or a version of it with the arguments made specific.
